title: Khoresh fesenjan
subtitle: Persian walnut and pomegranate stew
excerpt: One of the most distinctive dishes of Persian cooking: chicken braised in a rich sauce of ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses until dark, thick, and deeply sour-sweet. Served over saffron rice.
sourceNotes: Fesenjan is one of the oldest Persian dishes, with origins in Gilan province. Cross-referenced with Najmieh Batmanglij, Food of Life (2011).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. The sauce thickens on freezing; add a splash of water when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles easily. The stew improves with time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Excellent made a day ahead. The flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Fesenjan is built on two things: finely ground toasted walnuts and pomegranate molasses. The walnuts are ground almost to a paste, then cooked slowly with the chicken until the oil releases and the sauce turns very dark and thick. The flavour is sour, rich, and unlike anything else. Pomegranate molasses is available in Middle Eastern grocery shops and some supermarkets.

items.prepNote: skin-on or removed depending on preference
lightly toasted, then finely ground in a food processor
to balance, add more if the molasses is very sour

content.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan for 5 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Cool, then grind very finely in a food processor. Set aside.
In a large heavy casserole, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces in batches, 3 to 4 minutes each side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes until golden. Add the turmeric and cinnamon stick and cook for 1 minute.
Add the ground walnuts and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the stock and add the pomegranate molasses and sugar. Stir well. Return the chicken to the pot.

Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to very low. Cook, partially covered, for 1 hour, stirring every 20 minutes. The sauce will darken and thicken considerably. The walnut oil will rise to the surface; this is correct.

Taste and adjust: add more pomegranate molasses for sourness, more sugar for sweetness, salt as needed. The balance is the point. Remove the cinnamon stick. Serve over saffron rice, scattered with pomegranate seeds if available.

items.cause: Pomegranate molasses varies widely in acidity by brand
items.fix: Add sugar a teaspoon at a time, stirring and tasting. Some versions of fesenjan are quite sweet.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thin after 1 hour
items.cause: Too much stock or heat too low to reduce
items.fix: Remove the lid and cook for a further 15 to 20 minutes, stirring frequently.

items.symptom: The walnuts did not ground finely enough
items.fix: Process until the texture is very fine, almost paste-like. Coarse walnuts give a gritty sauce.

items.symptom: The oil pool on the surface is very large
items.cause: Normal walnut oil release; some varieties are oilier
items.fix: Skim off excess oil with a spoon before serving, or leave it as it is.

content.text: Fesenjan is ancient. The combination of walnuts and pomegranate appears in Persian texts from over a thousand years ago, and versions of this stew are found across Iran and into neighbouring countries. The original was made with duck; chicken is now the everyday version. Duck fesenjan is richer and darker still, cooked for longer. The dish is associated with celebrations and the autumn harvest when fresh pomegranates come in.
